body_ar:
بين أيدينا عدد من الصفات الفعلية المتقابلة، وكلها مما يدل على عظمة الله سبحانه وتعالى.
من صفات الله الفعلية:
يقول الشيخ حفظه الله: [يخفض يرفع يعز ويـذل يكره يمقت ويهدي ويضل] ما زلنا في ذكر بعض الصفات التي جاءت بالإثبات التفصيلي في كتاب الله وفي سنة رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم، فمنها: ......
إثبات صفة الخفض والرفع لله عز وجل:
(الخفض والرفع): فالله سبحانه وتعالى يخفض خفضاً حسياً وخفضاً معنوياً, فالخفض الحسي مثل خفض المنافقين في النار, حيث جعلهم تحت الكافرين فيها، ومثل خفضه لبعض المخلوقات عن بعض, فهذا هو الخفض الحسي، ومنه الخسف وغيره. وأما الخفض المعنوي: فهو مثل خفضه لمنزلة الكافرين في الدنيا وفي الآخرة، كخفضه في الدنيا لمنزلة أكثر الكافرين على أتباع عيسى بن مريم، فقد جعل أتباعه فوق الكافرين إلى يوم القيامة, فخفض الكافرين تحت رئاسة أتباع عيسى إلى يوم القيامة, كما تعهد بذلك لعيسى في قوله: وَجَاعِلُ الَّذِينَ اتَّبَعُوكَ فَوْقَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا إِلَى يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ [آل عمران:55]...
body_en:
*[Site synopsis]* Before us are a number of paired active attributes, all of them indicating the greatness of God, glorified and exalted is He.

## Some of God's active attributes

The Sheikh, may God preserve him, says:

*[He lowers, He raises; He honours and He abases; He dislikes, He detests; and He guides and He leads astray.]*

We are still in the mention of some of the attributes that come with detailed affirmation in the Book of God and in the Sunnah of His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace. Among them: ……

## Affirming the attributes of lowering and raising for God, mighty and majestic

"Lowering and raising": God, glorified and exalted is He, lowers with a lowering that is perceptible and a lowering that is not. Perceptible lowering is such as His lowering of the hypocrites in the Fire, where He has placed them beneath the disbelievers in it; and such as His lowering of some created things below others. This is perceptible lowering, and of it is the swallowing up of the earth and the like.

As for lowering that is not perceptible, it is such as His lowering of the standing of the disbelievers in this world and in the Hereafter — as His lowering, in this world, of the standing of most of the disbelievers below the followers of Jesus son of Mary. For He has placed his followers above the disbelievers until the Day of Resurrection, and so lowered the disbelievers beneath the leadership of the followers of Jesus until the Day of Resurrection, as He undertook to Jesus in His words: {and placing those who follow you above those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection} (Sūrat Āl ʿImrān 3:55)…

The opening paragraph is a synopsis written by the site, speaking about the lesson in the third person; everything from the section heading onward is the lecturer's own words as transcribed, together with the quoted line of the versified base text, which is his teacher's. The site must keep the voices apart.

flags.context: يخفض يرفع يعز ويـذل يكره يمقت ويهدي ويضل
flags.note: CRITICAL. 'يكره' here is a divine act — an attribute of God — and not the legal ruling makrūh. The five-rulings mapping of style guide section 3 must not be applied to it, and 'disliked (makrūh)' must never appear in this record. The same caution as the kalām exemption in section 8: check the subject before applying the mapping. A ruling attaches to an act; this attaches to God. Flagged because the word is the single highest-risk token in the whole 734-747 run.

options: translate faithfully and hold for editorial decision
flags.note: Style guide section 12. This is exegesis of Sūrat Āl ʿImrān 3:55 and is unremarkable within the genre, but in English, standing alone on a page with no surrounding argument, it reads as a ranking of religious communities and of Christians in particular, and carries reputational exposure in several jurisdictions. Translated faithfully, neither softened nor strengthened. Whether and how to publish is for Ummah Collective and the Sheikh's office.

flags.context: فقد جعل أتباعه فوق الكافرين إلى يوم القيامة
flags.note: The Arabic says 'followers of Jesus' and not 'Christians', and in this genre the phrase is often read as covering those who followed him truly rather than the historical Christian communities. The record breaks off before the Sheikh says which he means, so the literal rendering is kept and no identification is supplied.

translator_notes: One of a run of fourteen records, IDs 734-747, the series 'The Names and Attributes', all built to the same template and all excerpts. Each carries a site-written synopsis, then a section heading, then the opening formula and the first lines of a lesson, and then breaks off on an ellipsis; the full text sits behind a .doc download in the /medias/doc/esmawesivat-* series, numbered 1 to 14 in the same order as the IDs.

The source's final line, 'تحميل المادة' ('download the material'), is the label of a download link in the page furniture, not part of the text. It is recorded as source_download_link and omitted from body_ar and body_en.

This record does carry a CMS timestamp in a .create_date span (10 May 2011, within a 28-minute window shared by the whole run 738-747). That is a bulk-upload timestamp for the series, not the date the lesson was given, and it is not evidence of composition date. Record 737, translated in an earlier wave, reports no date for this run; the timestamp is in fact present in the page and should be backfilled there.
Qur'anic renderings here are interpretive and are not a substitute for the Arabic.
Creedal material. Per style guide section 8, the vocabulary of divine attributes is not the vocabulary of the five legal rulings and the five-rulings mapping is not applied anywhere in this record.

Eight attributes are named in the quoted line and only the first pair is expounded before the record stops. Marked critical_for_display: in particular 'He guides and He leads astray' is left standing with no treatment at all, which is the point in this material at which a reader is most likely to supply a position the Sheikh has not given.

'حسي / معنوي' is rendered 'perceptible' and 'not perceptible' rather than 'physical' and 'spiritual' or 'literal' and 'metaphorical': the Arabic pair is about what the senses can register, and the English alternatives would import a position on the divine attributes that this passage does not take.
'الخسف' is rendered 'the swallowing up of the earth', the Qur'anic sense, rather than 'eclipse', which is the other sense of the root and is not meant here.
